title: Criticism over undisclosed public-affairs (lobbying) clients while serving as Ständerat
description: After taking a position as Senior Advisor Public Affairs at the Zurich agency IRF Reputation AG in early 2025, and especially following his October 2025 election as FDP co-president, Mühlemann faced criticism that he had not disclosed which clients he advises. Under parliamentary transparency rules he must declare his employer but not the employer's clients. The transparency NGO Lobbywatch and media outlets (Infosperber, Republik, Südostschweiz) called the arrangement problematic, noting that voters cannot see which private interests he may represent. Mühlemann stated that IRF does not provide information about its clients. He has not been accused of any rule violation.
